rv.q: This is because Lloyd’s using Colin Teevan’s recent adaptation of the text for the West Yorkshire Playhouse, which dispenses with the middle section and splices in new scenes.

But those portions are now most of the play – the effect is more like a gleeful graffiti-ing of Doctor Faustus Marlowe or a play ‘after Marlowe’ than an update. At times it feels wilfully incoherent – though much about it is compelling.

Game of Thrones star Kit Harington is agile and energetic in this unapologetically messy take on Christopher Marlowe’s classic play. He doesn’t always make perfect sense of the passionate Elizabethan verse, but he has an undeniable presence. When we first see his masochistic Faustus, he’s a nerd in a hoodie, glued to his computer.

Colin Teevan replaces Marlowe’s unappetising middle section with some incoherent satire. The stage gibbers with spirits writhing around in grubby knickers. Jenna Russell is an acid, wheedling Mephistopheles, who provides an uplifting rendition of Bat out of Hell.
